importance_ranking.reason: Visual variation across building sub-types is significant — an industrial clear-span warehouse, a curved-roof commercial structure, a cold storage building, and a modular site office are visually distinct. Buyers use the image to confirm building type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Frame type, eave height, span, and cladding material are non-interchangeable structural parameters. A buyer needing a 30m clear-span warehouse cannot evaluate a listing that does not disclose these specs — they are the primary shortlisting gate.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised manufacturers — Interarch, Everest Industries, Kirby Building Systems, Zamil Steel — are specified by name by institutional buyers, large EPC contractors, and architects evaluating vendor credentials for capital projects.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a high-value capital project where IS:800 compliance, ISO 9001 certification, in-house structural design capability, and erection track record are evaluated during vendor selection. Seller identity is a significant trust signal, though specs carry equal weight in initial shortlisting.

Every PEB is custom-designed and project-quoted; no fixed catalogue price exists. Indicative per-sq-ft rates are used by Indian buyers for budget benchmarking, but final price is always negotiated after structural design is confirmed. Price is a qualification signal after spec and company evaluation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Three quoting conventions coexist in this MCAT: per sq ft (turnkey/area-based), per MT (supply-only steel components), and per project (lump-sum turnkey). A buyer comparing listings without unit clarity will misread prices significantly — per sq ft and per MT are not interchangeable price signals.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit must be shown because per sq ft, per MT, and per project are all active quoting conventions in this MCAT. Price comparison is meaningless without unit clarity — this is a genuine buyer confusion risk, not a theoretical one.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Frame type defines the structural system — clear span, multi-span, portal frame, and curved roof are non-interchangeable configurations that drive primary steel tonnage and therefore the largest component of project price.

Eave height directly determines steel tonnage and structural complexity — a 15m eave height building requires substantially heavier primary frames than a 6m building of the same footprint, creating a significant and non-substitutable price delta.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Clear span (column-free width) is the single most critical structural parameter for a PEB — it determines primary frame weight, steel grade, and project price more than any other dimension, and buyers specify it as a non-negotiable requirement for their floor plan.

Single-skin colour-coated sheet, sandwich/PUF panel, and bare purlin represent major price and thermal performance differences — cold storage and temperature-controlled buildings require insulated panels while standard warehouses use single-skin sheets, making this a primary cost driver.

IS:1893 seismic zone and IS:875 wind zone are mandatory design inputs under Indian standards — they determine structural steel grade, connection design, and foundation loads, and institutional/government buyers specify zone compliance as a procurement requirement.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Application type routes the RFQ to sellers who specialise in the right building category — a cold storage specialist, an industrial shed fabricator, and a modular site office supplier are distinct seller types who cannot respond accurately without knowing the intended use.

Total area defines project scale and allows sellers to determine whether the project is within their capacity and to provide a meaningful indicative quote — a seller specialising in large industrial PEBs cannot respond usefully to a 500 sq ft site office enquiry.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need the required column-free span to determine frame type, primary steel tonnage, and project price — a buyer needing 30m clear span requires a fundamentally different structural solution than one needing 12m, and total area alone does not capture this.
